items.title: Firebird Proxy rejects SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT and RELEASE SAVEPOINT
A failed `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` leaves the connection in a transaction
items.body:
`transactionDepth` changes only after a transaction statement succeeds. When `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` fails, the depth stays one level too high. The outer commit sends `RELEASE SAVEPOINT` instead of `COMMIT`. The query runner is released while the connection is still in a transaction. The next unit of work on that connection commits rows the application was told were rolled back.

This includes a `beforeTransactionRollback` subscriber that throws. No driver patch is required for that case. The rollback fails before the statement is sent.

### Expected Behavior

The nested `transaction()` rejects with the rollback error. The enclosing `transaction()` also rejects, because it may still contain the rows that rollback was supposed to discard. The managed enclosing transaction attempts a rollback at the correct level, rather than committing those rows or releasing a connection because its logical depth is wrong. If that final rollback fails, connection disposal is a separate problem. A successful rollback of an enclosing savepoint discards the failed one, and the transaction outside that savepoint can commit. A savepoint opened after the failure can commit. The scope that still contains the failure cannot.

### Actual Behavior

Pool of one connection. The inner callback throws, the caller catches that error, and the outer callback returns.

Injected, client: `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` is rejected and is not sent. The outer `transaction()` resolves. No `COMMIT` is sent. The connection is idle in a transaction. The next unit of work commits `outer` and `inner-doomed`.

Injected, server: the savepoint rollback is sent with a savepoint name that does not exist. On PostgreSQL the server returns `3B001` and aborts the transaction. The outer call rejects, but the managed rollback sends `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT typeorm_1` instead of `ROLLBACK`. The connection is idle in a transaction. The next unit of work commits `outer`.

The same result follows from a `beforeTransactionRollback` subscriber that throws. Nothing is injected.

### Steps to reproduce

TypeORM 1.1.2, PostgreSQL, `poolSize: 1`.

```ts
await dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {
    await manager.save(Post, { title: "outer" })
    await manager
        .transaction(async (inner) => {
            await inner.save(Post, { title: "inner-doomed" })
            throw new Error("inner unit failed")
        })
        .catch(() => undefined)
})

await dataSource.transaction((manager) =>
    manager.save(Post, { title: "next-request" }),
)
```

To make the inner `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` fail before it is sent, reject that statement in the client and do not send it. That part is injected. The subscriber case needs no injection: throw from `beforeTransactionRollback` on the nested rollback.

After the first call, a second connection sees no rows. After the second call it sees `outer`, `inner-doomed`, and `next-request`.

### My Environment

| Dependency | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Operating System | macOS arm64 |
| Node.js version | 24 |
| TypeORM version | 1.1.2 (master `fe923942`) |
| PostgreSQL | 17.11 |
| MySQL | 9.5.0 |
| MariaDB | 12.2.2 |
| CockroachDB | 24.3.8 |

### Additional Context

Depth moves after the statement on purpose, so a failure cannot drive the depth negative (#11264). Decrementing the depth in a `finally`, without remembering the failure, turns the outer commit into a real `COMMIT` of `inner-doomed`. On PostgreSQL that `COMMIT` can also return the `ROLLBACK` tag and still resolve.

Releasing a query runner that is still inside a transaction is a separate bug. This report is the depth and the commit that follow a failed savepoint rollback.

Relevant drivers: postgres, aurora-postgres, cockroachdb, mysql, mariadb, aurora-mysql, better-sqlite3, sqljs, sqlite, capacitor, expo, nativescript, react-native, oracle, sqlserver.

I am willing to resolve this with a pull request.

items.title: Transactions report success when PostgreSQL did not commit, and after('commit') hooks run without a commit
fix(query-runner): prevent committing after failed savepoint rollback and align transaction depth
items.body:
### Description of change

Fixes #12977.

#### Context & Problem
When a nested transaction rollback to a savepoint fails (for instance, when a \BeforeTransactionRollback\ subscriber throws, or when the database rejects the \ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT\ statement), \	ransactionDepth\ previously remained unchanged because depth decrementing occurred only after statement execution.

This led to two critical issues:
1. **Silent Data Leak & Corrupt Commits**: If the caller caught the inner error and the outer callback returned normally, \commitTransaction()\ checked \	his.transactionDepth > 1\, which evaluated to \	rue\. Consequently, it sent \RELEASE SAVEPOINT\ instead of \COMMIT\, leaving the connection in an active transaction block. When returned to the pool, subsequent requests on that connection would commit dirty rows that were assumed to be rolled back.
2. **Desynchronized Managed Rollbacks**: If the outer transaction subsequently aborted and attempted a rollback, it ran at an inflated depth (e.g. depth 2 instead of depth 1), issuing \ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT typeorm_1\ instead of issuing \ROLLBACK\ to terminate the root transaction block.

#### Solution
1. **Depth Realignment on Failed Rollback**:
   In \ollbackTransaction()\, wrapped the rollback statement and broadcaster in a \	ry...catch\. On error at \currentDepth > 1\, decrement \	his.transactionDepth = currentDepth - 1\ to realign the runner's logical depth with the enclosing transaction scope.
2. **Contamination Tracking via \ ailedRollbackDepth\**:
   Introduced \protected failedRollbackDepth?: number\ in \BaseQueryRunner\. When a nested rollback fails, \ ailedRollbackDepth\ records the minimum depth of the contaminated scope. If \commitTransaction()\ is subsequently called at or below this depth, it immediately throws a \TypeORMError\ rather than committing data that was doomed to rollback.
3. **Savepoint Discard Semantics**:
   - If an enclosing savepoint successfully rolls back (\	ransactionDepth < failedRollbackDepth\), all intermediate changes (including the failed savepoint's modifications) are discarded by the database, resetting \ ailedRollbackDepth = undefined\ and allowing the outer scope to commit safely.
   - Newly opened savepoints (\	ransactionDepth > failedRollbackDepth\) can commit normally, while the enclosing contaminated scope remains blocked from committing.
4. **All Relational Drivers Covered**:
   Updated all query runners implementing nested transaction savepoints: \PostgresQueryRunner\, \MysqlQueryRunner\, \AbstractSqliteQueryRunner\, \AuroraMysqlQueryRunner\, \AuroraPostgresQueryRunner\, \CockroachQueryRunner\, \OracleQueryRunner\, and \SqlServerQueryRunner\.

#### Verification
Added comprehensive test suite in \packages/typeorm/test/github-issues/12977/issue-12977.test.ts\ covering 5 distinct scenarios:
1. Preventing outer transaction commit and ensuring clean rollback when a nested rollback fails.
2. Verifying depth realignment and clean root \ROLLBACK\ when an inner rollback fails without being caught.
3. Allowing outer transaction commit when an enclosing savepoint rolls back successfully.
4. Allowing a savepoint opened after the failure to commit while preventing the contaminated outer scope from committing.
5. Direct \QueryRunner\ unit verification of \	ransactionDepth\ transitions, commit rejection, and root \isTransactionActive\ clearance.

### Pull-Request Checklist

- [x] Code is up-to-date with the \master\ branch
- [x] This pull request links a relevant issue using a closing keyword: \Fixes #12977\
- [x] There are new or updated tests validating the change (\	ests/**.test.ts\)
- [x] Documentation has been updated to reflect this change (\docs/docs/**.md\ - N/A)

items.title: postgres-js: a refusal recovered through a raw savepoint fails the caller's transaction at commit
BUG #19782: SET CONSTRAINTS in a released savepoint survives ROLLBACK TO an enclosing savepoint
items.body:
> **Read-only mirror.** Report and reply on pgsql-bugs; activity here is not sent upstream.

- Original author: PG Bug reporting form <noreply(at)postgresql(dot)org>
- Mailing list: `pgsql-bugs`
- Message-ID: `19782-02b66fb19c9ce85b@postgresql.org`
- [Original email](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/19782-02b66fb19c9ce85b%40postgresql.org)

---

The following bug has been logged on the website:
Bug reference:      19782
Logged by:          Alperen Keles
Email address:      alpkeles99(at)gmail(dot)com
PostgreSQL version: 14.24
Operating system:   macOS 26 arm64
Description:
Hello,
SET CONSTRAINTS run in a savepoint is undone by ROLLBACK TO that
savepoint. But if it runs in an inner savepoint that is then released,
a ROLLBACK TO the enclosing savepoint does not undo it, and the
constraints keep the mode the rolled-back command gave them.
  CREATE TABLE p (k int PRIMARY KEY);
  CREATE TABLE c (f int CONSTRAINT c_f REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE);
  BEGIN;
  SAVEPOINT s0;
  SAVEPOINT s1;
  SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;
  RELEASE s1;
  ROLLBACK TO s0;
  INSERT INTO c VALUES (99);    -- INSERT 0 1: c_f is still deferred
  COMMIT;
  ERROR:  insert or update on table "c" violates foreign key constraint
"c_f"
  DETAIL:  Key (f)=(99) is not present in table "p".
Without the inner savepoint the INSERT fails right away, as expected:
  BEGIN;
  SAVEPOINT s0;
  SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;
  ROLLBACK TO s0;
  INSERT INTO c VALUES (99);
  ERROR:  insert or update on table "c" violates foreign key constraint
"c_f"
RELEASE SAVEPOINT merges s1's changes into s0, and ROLLBACK TO s0 rolls
back all commands executed after s0 was established, so the two cases
should behave the same: c_f should be immediate again after ROLLBACK TO
s0.
It works in the other direction too. With a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY
DEFERRED foreign key, SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE in a released inner
savepoint survives ROLLBACK TO s0, so a transaction that inserts the
child row before the parent row fails at the first INSERT even though
it would commit without the savepoints:
  CREATE TABLE d (f int CONSTRAINT d_f REFERENCES p
                  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED);
  BEGIN;
  SAVEPOINT s0;
  SAVEPOINT s1;
  SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE;
  RELEASE s1;
  ROLLBACK TO s0;
  INSERT INTO d VALUES (5);
  ERROR:  insert or update on table "d" violates foreign key constraint
"d_f"
  INSERT INTO p VALUES (5);
  ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of
transaction block
The same happens with SET CONSTRAINTS by name, with deferrable UNIQUE
and EXCLUDE constraints, at deeper nesting (the SET in s2, RELEASE s2,
then ROLLBACK TO s1 or s0), and with PL/pgSQL exception blocks, which
are subtransactions too: an inner block that runs SET CONSTRAINTS ALL
DEFERRED and exits normally, inside an outer block whose exception is
caught, leaves the constraints deferred; so does calling a function
whose exception block runs SET CONSTRAINTS inside a savepoint that is
then rolled back. A ROLLBACK of the whole transaction is not affected.
I could not get a violating row committed this way: the wrongly
deferred check still runs at COMMIT, which fails. The effect is that
the check happens at the wrong statement, so an error that the
application expects to catch at the INSERT (with a savepoint or an
exception handler) aborts the whole transaction at COMMIT instead, or,
in the IMMEDIATE direction, a valid transaction is rejected.
Reproduced on 14.24 (REL_14_STABLE b1c44848ce3), 18.6 (REL_18_STABLE
a85b5523e67), 19rc1 (REL_19_STABLE 0fb192f1b02) and master dd568b047ac
(2026-10-21),
macOS arm64, all --enable-cassert.
As far as I can tell, the cause is in trigger.c. The SET CONSTRAINTS
state is saved for a subtransaction level only when SET CONSTRAINTS
runs at that level (AfterTriggerSetState copies it into
trans_stack[my_level].state). When the inner level commits,
AfterTriggerEndSubXact frees its saved copy ("If we saved a prior
state, we don't need it anymore") and does not pass it to the parent
level, whose slot is still NULL. So when the parent level aborts, it
finds nothing to restore ("If the saved state is NULL, then this
subxact didn't save it, so it doesn't need restoring"). The code
seems to date from the nested transactions commit (573a71a5da7, 8.0).
Found with a query fuzzer.
Regards,
Alperen Keles

items.title: Whitelisted wrappers that catch a post-write exception and return OperationResult.fail commit the partial write anyway (~55-file grep, unverified population)
items.body:
## What this is

A class-level discovery made while fixing #1325's TOCTOU-closing follow-up (PR fixing
#1325, commit adding a savepoint to `member_merge_service.execute_merge`'s whitelisted
wrapper). Filing per the "a finding is a class, not an instance" rule before closing
that work out.

## The shape

`verenigingen/services/member_merge_service.py`'s whitelisted `execute_merge` used to
catch `frappe.ValidationError` (raised by a check that can run AFTER `target.save()`)
and return a normal `OperationResult.fail(...)` dict, with no `frappe.db.rollback()` /
savepoint rollback anywhere in that except branch. Measured directly against
`frappe/app.py`: when no exception escapes `frappe.handler.handle()`, the request is
treated as successful and `sync_database()` runs `db.commit(chain=True)` for an "unsafe"
HTTP method (POST) regardless of what the callee returned. So a whitelisted endpoint
that:

1. performs a write (`.save()`/`.insert()`/`.submit()`/`db_set()`),
2. later hits a code path that raises,
3. catches that exception itself and returns `OperationResult.fail(...)` (or any other
   "this failed" dict) without rolling back,

will have that write **silently committed anyway** by the outer request-completion
layer, because the request "succeeded" from Frappe's point of view even though the
caller was told it failed.

member_merge_service.py's own copy of this bug is fixed (savepoint taken before the
call, rolled back to on every post-write except branch, released on success).

## What is NOT established

**A raw grep, not a verified population.** `grep -rln "OperationResult.fail" services/
api/` returns approximately **55 files**. That count answers "how many files return this
shape at all," not "how many actually write-then-catch-and-return-fail with no
rollback" -- most `OperationResult.fail` sites are ordinary validation-before-any-write
failures (immune to this, same as #1325's own now-fixed FIRST check), and some route
through a `ValidationResult`-returning service layer rather than catching an exception
directly at the whitelisted boundary, which would need its own trace to classify either
way.

Two files were spot-checked, NOT fully traced end-to-end:

- `services/payment/sepa_mandate_manager.py` -- `create_mandate_api` (~1421) doesn't
  itself catch a post-write exception (it dispatches to `manager.create_mandate(...)`,
  which returns a `ValidationResult` rather than raising); whether that inner method's
  OWN code path can write and then report `valid=False` without rolling back is what
  would need tracing next.
- `services/member/approval/member_approval_service.py` -- similarly has saves and
  `OperationResult.fail` returns in the same module; not traced call-by-call for whether
  any single request path does write-then-catch-then-fail-without-rollback.

Neither spot-check is a confirmed instance of the bug -- they are candidates for the
next pass, recorded so the 55-file grep isn't mistaken for 55 confirmed exposures.

## Suggested approach for whoever picks this up

- Don't fix by inspection file-by-file; the pattern is easy to miss by reading (that's
  how #1325's own second check needed a savepoint at all). Prefer an AST or grep sweep
  for "a whitelisted function's `except` block returns without a preceding
  `rollback`/`rollback_to_savepoint` call, and the function body upstream of that except
  contains a `.save(`/`.insert(`/`.submit(`/`db_set(`" -- matching the shape, not the
  symptom.
- `verenigingen/utils/transaction_errors.py` (`rollback_to_savepoint`,
  `release_savepoint_if_present`, `atomic_status_transition`) is the existing, load-bearing
  toolkit for this -- reuse it rather than re-deriving the 1305-tolerance logic in each
  fix (see #1325's PR for the pattern: a savepoint before the write-capable call, rolled
  back on every post-write except branch, released on success).

Related: #1325 (where this was found and fixed for one call site), #1361 (a sibling
"same shape, ~70 more sites" sweep for a different swallow class -- same STANDING rule:
grep the pattern, not the instance), #958 (a bare `except Exception` flattening a
retryable deadlock into a permanent domain error -- adjacent failure mode: that one
mis-reports the type of failure, this one mis-reports whether a write happened at all).

items.title: BaseService.rollback_transaction() is an unguarded savepoint rollback invisible to the #561 AST ratchet (helper-indirection blind spot)
items.body:
## What is established

#561's AST ratchet (`verenigingen/tests/unit/test_savepoint_rollback_cannot_mask_the_error.py`)
scans every production `except` handler for a hand-written savepoint rollback
(`frappe.db.rollback(save_point=...)` or raw `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` SQL) that
should go through `rollback_to_savepoint()` instead, plus a missing
`except NON_RESUMABLE_DB_ERRORS: raise` above a swallowing catch-all. It walks
each handler's own AST subtree (`ast.walk(handler)`).

That walk has a real blind spot, found while doing the class sweep for PR
#1171's two newly-fixed sites: **a handler that calls a separately-defined
helper method, and that helper's OWN body does the bare rollback, is
invisible to the ratchet** -- the handler's AST only contains a `Call` node
for the method invocation (e.g. `self.rollback_transaction()`), not the
method's body, which lives in a different function definition elsewhere in
the file.

`verenigingen/services/infrastructure/base_service.py`'s `BaseService` class
has exactly this shape, in TWO places:

```python
def rollback_transaction(self):
    """Roll back to the savepoint, undoing only this nested transaction."""
    if self._transaction_active:
        if self._savepoint_name:
            frappe.db.rollback(save_point=self._savepoint_name)   # <-- bare, UNPROTECTED
        ...

def execute_with_transaction(self, operation_func, *args, **kwargs):
    ...
    try:
        result = operation_func(*args, **kwargs)
        self.commit_transaction()
        ...
        return result
    except Exception as e:                    # <-- no NON_RESUMABLE_DB_ERRORS guard above this
        self.rollback_transaction()            # <-- calls the bare rollback above
        self._end_operation(operation_name, start_time, success=False)
        self.handle_error(e, operation_name, {"args": args, "kwargs": kwargs})
```

and again in a bulk-batch method (~line 585-599):

```python
try:
    for item in batch:
        operation_func(item)
        processed += 1
    self.commit_transaction()
    ...
except Exception as e:
    self.rollback_transaction()
    error_msg = f"Batch {i // batch_size + 1} failed: {str(e)}"
    errors.append(error_msg)     # swallowed -- no re-raise at all, loop continues
    self.logger.error(error_msg)
```

Unlike the two sites fixed in PR #1171, `rollback_transaction()` has **zero**
protection: it is not even wrapped in its own try/except tolerating the
"savepoint already gone" 1305 the way
`termination_execution_service._rollback_savepoint` is (that one IS correctly
marked `# non-resumable-ok:` and is not a false negative). A 1213 deadlock or
a nested commit reaching either of these two `except Exception` blocks will
have `rollback_transaction()` raise 1305 straight out of the handler,
replacing the original exception -- in `execute_with_transaction`'s case,
propagating a masked error to the caller; in the bulk-batch case, the 1305
propagates UNCAUGHT out of the whole loop (worse than the "swallow and
continue" the surrounding code clearly intends), since there is no further
handler to catch it.

`BaseService`/`StatefulService` is not a toy class: grepped for real
subclasses (excluding tests) and found 7:
`customer_handling_service.CustomerHandlingService`,
`approval/contribution_amendment_approval_service.ContributionAmendmentApprovalService`,
`approval/termination_approval_service.TerminationApprovalService`,
`billing/bulk_invoice_generation_service.BulkInvoiceGenerationService`,
`mijnrood_sync/services/application_approval_correlator.ApplicationApprovalCorrelator`,
`mijnrood_sync/services/polling_service.MijnRoodPollingService`,
`mijnrood_sync/services/event_application/dispatcher.MijnRoodEventApplicationService`.
None override `rollback_transaction`/`commit_transaction`/`execute_with_transaction`,
so all inherit this exact shape if they ever call `execute_with_transaction()`
or the bulk-batch method.

## App-wide census (grep, not just the ratchet)

Grepped `frappe.db.rollback(save_point=` and raw `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`
across `verenigingen/` AND `scripts/` (the ratchet's own `APP_ROOT` only
covers the former -- ratchets hardcoding a `verenigingen` root missing
`scripts/` is a known recurring class in this repo, though `scripts/` came
back clean this time):

| file | bare `rollback(save_point=...)` occurrences | shape |
|---|---|---|
| `services/infrastructure/base_service.py` | 1 (inside `rollback_transaction()`) | **unguarded helper, called from 2 unguarded `except` blocks -- THE FINDING** |
| `services/payment/sepa_upload_guard.py` | 1 | try-body early return (no exception in flight) -- fine, and its actual `except` handlers already use `rollback_to_savepoint` + `NON_RESUMABLE_DB_ERRORS` |
| `services/termination/termination_execution_service.py` | 1 | inside `_rollback_savepoint()`, itself wrapped in its own try/except with `# non-resumable-ok:` -- correctly exempt |
| `services/member/account/base_role_profile_manager.py` | 9 | all try-body early returns; its 5 real `except` handlers already use `rollback_to_savepoint` + `NON_RESUMABLE_DB_ERRORS` |
| `utils/transaction_errors.py` | 1 | the canonical helper's own implementation |
| `scripts/**` | 0 | clean |

Raw `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` SQL: 0 live occurrences anywhere (the 4 grep hits
are all comments/docstrings referencing the historical, now-fixed shape).

So the class sweep finds exactly **one** root cause beyond the two fixed in
PR #1171: `BaseService.rollback_transaction()`'s two call sites.

## What is NOT established

- Whether either `execute_with_transaction()` or the bulk-batch method is
  actually reached by a live caller with a real 1213/1205 today (not traced
  per-subclass; would need checking each of the 7 subclasses' own callers).
- Whether any subclass's `operation_func`/`handle_error` already provides
  its own downstream protection that would blunt the practical impact.

## Suggested next step

Fix `BaseService.rollback_transaction()` and the bulk-batch handler the same
way PR #1171 fixed the other two sites: route through `rollback_to_savepoint()`
(or `release_savepoint_if_present()` on `commit_transaction()`'s mirror path),
and add `except NON_RESUMABLE_DB_ERRORS: raise` above both `except Exception`
blocks. Since this is a shared base class, one fix covers all 7 subclasses.
Worth also asking whether the AST ratchet itself should be extended to catch
the "handler calls a helper whose body is savepoint-only" shape generally
(it already has one bespoke carve-out for
`termination_execution_service._rollback_savepoint` via
`_hand_written_copies`, but that rule matches "the WHOLE try body is savepoint
work", not "a handler calls out to another method that does it") -- flagged
here, not solved.

## Related

- #1143 / #1171 -- the PR whose class sweep surfaced this while fixing the
  two `frappe.db.begin()`-adjacent savepoint sites the second-round review
  found.
- #561 -- the original savepoint-masking defect and its ratchet.

items.title: bug #19782: set constraints in a released savepoint survives rollback to an enclosing savepoint
items.body:
**📨 Subject**: BUG #19782: SET CONSTRAINTS in a released savepoint survives ROLLBACK TO an enclosing savepoint

**📅 Date:** 2026-10-21 18:25:09
**📤 Sender:** PG Bug reporting form <noreply(at)postgresql(dot)org>
**📥 Receiver:** pgsql-bugs(at)lists(dot)postgresql(dot)org
**📮 Message ID:** `19782-02b66fb19c9ce85b@postgresql.org`

**📝 Message :**
The following bug has been logged on the website:

Bug reference: 19782  
Logged by: Alperen Keles  
Email address: alpkeles99(at)gmail(dot)com  
PostgreSQL version: 14.24  
Operating system: macOS 26 arm64  
Description:

SET CONSTRAINTS run in a savepoint is undone by ROLLBACK TO that  
savepoint. But if it runs in an inner savepoint that is then released,  
a ROLLBACK TO the enclosing savepoint does not undo it, and the  
constraints keep the mode the rolled-back command gave them.

CREATE TABLE p (k int PRIMARY KEY);  
CREATE TABLE c (f int CONSTRAINT c_f REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE);

BEGIN;  
SAVEPOINT s0;  
SAVEPOINT s1;  
SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;  
RELEASE s1;  
ROLLBACK TO s0;  
INSERT INTO c VALUES (99); -- INSERT 0 1: c_f is still deferred  
COMMIT;  
ERROR: insert or update on table "c" violates foreign key constraint  
"c_f"  
DETAIL: Key (f)=(99) is not present in table "p".

Without the inner savepoint the INSERT fails right away, as expected:

BEGIN;  
SAVEPOINT s0;  
SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;  
ROLLBACK TO s0;  
INSERT INTO c VALUES (99);  
ERROR: insert or update on table "c" violates foreign key constraint  
"c_f"

RELEASE SAVEPOINT merges s1's changes into s0, and ROLLBACK TO s0 rolls  
back all commands executed after s0 was established, so the two cases  
should behave the same: c_f should be immediate again after ROLLBACK TO  
s0.

It works in the other direction too. With a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY  
DEFERRED foreign key, SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE in a released inner  
savepoint survives ROLLBACK TO s0, so a transaction that inserts the

it would commit without the savepoints:

CREATE TABLE d (f int CONSTRAINT d_f REFERENCES p  
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED);  
BEGIN;  
SAVEPOINT s0;  
SAVEPOINT s1;  
SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE;  
RELEASE s1;  
ROLLBACK TO s0;  
INSERT INTO d VALUES (5);  
ERROR: insert or update on table "d" violates foreign key constraint  
"d_f"  
INSERT INTO p VALUES (5);  
ERROR: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of  
transaction block

The same happens with SET CONSTRAINTS by name, with deferrable UNIQUE  
and EXCLUDE constraints, at deeper nesting (the SET in s2, RELEASE s2,  
then ROLLBACK TO s1 or s0), and with PL/pgSQL exception blocks, which  
are subtransactions too: an inner block that runs SET CONSTRAINTS ALL  
DEFERRED and exits normally, inside an outer block whose exception is  
caught, leaves the constraints deferred; so does calling a function  
whose exception block runs SET CONSTRAINTS inside a savepoint that is  
then rolled back. A ROLLBACK of the whole transaction is not affected.

I could not get a violating row committed this way: the wrongly  
deferred check still runs at COMMIT, which fails. The effect is that  
the check happens at the wrong statement, so an error that the  
application expects to catch at the INSERT (with a savepoint or an  
exception handler) aborts the whole transaction at COMMIT instead, or,  
in the IMMEDIATE direction, a valid transaction is rejected.

Reproduced on 14.24 (REL_14_STABLE b1c44848ce3), 18.6 (REL_18_STABLE  
a85b5523e67), 19rc1 (REL_19_STABLE 0fb192f1b02) and master dd568b047ac  
(2026-10-21),  
macOS arm64, all --enable-cassert.

As far as I can tell, the cause is in trigger.c. The SET CONSTRAINTS  
state is saved for a subtransaction level only when SET CONSTRAINTS  
runs at that level (AfterTriggerSetState copies it into  
trans_stack[my_level].state). When the inner level commits,  
AfterTriggerEndSubXact frees its saved copy ("If we saved a prior  
state, we don't need it anymore") and does not pass it to the parent  
level, whose slot is still NULL. So when the parent level aborts, it  
finds nothing to restore ("If the saved state is NULL, then this  
subxact didn't save it, so it doesn't need restoring"). The code  
seems to date from the nested transactions commit (573a71a5da7, 8.0).

Found with a query fuzzer.

Regards,  
Alperen Keles
